title: Power Pages: site analytics and server logging configuration
summary: Pass with documentation gaps: the roadmap facts and published configuration routes are supported. Microsoft does not explicitly support the blanket assurance that the feature has no autonomous actions; the IP-retention and dashboard descriptions also need narrower qualifications.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Makers configure the planned analytics by opening the setup workspace and adding the analytics provider script.
claims.quote: To configure site analytics, makers must open the setup workspace and add the analytics provider script to enable traffic analytics.

claims.claim: The feature is enabled by admins, makers or marketers for end users.
claims.quote: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

claims.claim: Enablement is maker-selected, consistent with user-opt-in rather than a documented separate tenant admin gate.
claims.quote: To configure site analytics, makers must open the setup workspace and add the analytics provider script to enable traffic analytics.

claims.claim: No separate tenant administrator switch is documented for the planned analytics capability as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages analytics server logging tenant wide policy disable analytics admin switch. Read telemetry-monitoring, tenant-level-analytics and tenant-settings; the documented platform analytics switch concerns Power Apps/Power Automate reports, not this capability.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes, cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Application Insights uses Azure consumption billing based on telemetry data volume.
claims.quote: Because workspace-based Application Insights resources store their data in a Log Analytics workspace, the billing for data ingestion and retention is done by the workspace where the Application Insights data is located.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/cost-logs#application-insights-billing for the consumption model, Azure billing and ingestion-volume cost statements.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Pages licensing or a separate charge specific to this planned feature is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages configure site analytics server logging Application Insights licensing prerequisites log fields; "Power Pages" "analytics" "licensing" "Application Insights". Read FAQ, assign-licensing and Power Platform licensing FAQ excerpts; none states feature-specific licensing.

claims.claim: Learn already documents Power Pages diagnostic logging.
claims.quote: To get the website error logs into your Azure Blob storage, you must enable diagnostic logging from the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Learn documents a Power Pages DevTools extension that displays server-side errors.
claims.quote: It offers features such as displaying Liquid tracing message and server-side error messages.

claims.claim: UserTrace/Debug is a site setting used to enable diagnostic tracing for a site.
claims.quote: To enable the diagnostic setting for a public website: 1. Open the Power Pages Management App. 2. Add or update the Site Setting with the name UserTrace/Debug. 3. Set the value to true.

claims.claim: Application Insights masks IP addresses in stored telemetry by default.
claims.quote: By default, IP addresses are temporarily collected but not stored. ... The address is then discarded, and 0.0.0.0 is written to the client_IP field.

claims.claim: Retaining IP addresses requires setting the Application Insights component's DisableIpMasking property to true.
claims.quote: To enable IP collection and storage, the DisableIpMasking property of the Application Insights component must be set to true. ... DisableIpMasking applies to classic Application Insights ingestion.
claims.fix: Replace the retaining-addresses clause with: 'For classic Application Insights ingestion, retaining IP addresses requires setting DisableIpMasking to true; native OTLP ingestion does not retain the address regardless of that property.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The exact fields of the planned server and access logs have not yet been documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages configure site analytics server logging Application Insights licensing prerequisites log fields. Read roadmap, devtools-addon, view-portal-error-log and telemetry-monitoring; none specifies the planned server/access-log schema.

claims.claim: Azure roles govern access to Application Insights resources.
claims.quote: Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) provides built-in roles for monitoring to assign to users, groups, service principals, and managed identities. ... Access Application Insights data.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/fundamentals/roles-permissions-security for the Azure resource-access claim.

claims.claim: The feature has no autonomous actions and only observes and reports.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "site analytics" "server logging" autonomous actions. Read roadmap, devtools-addon, view-portal-error-log and telemetry-monitoring; they describe telemetry and debugging, not an exhaustive assurance of no autonomous actions.
claims.fix: Replace 'None. The feature observes and reports.' with 'The roadmap describes telemetry and analytics, not autonomous remediation.'

claims.claim: Diagnostic Blob logging is configured in Power Platform admin center at Resources > Power Pages sites > site > Site Actions > Enable diagnostics logs.
claims.quote: Open the Power Platform admin center. ... Under the Resources section, select Power Pages sites. ... Select your website. ... From the Site Actions menu, select Enable diagnostics logs.

Read tenant-level-analytics, tenant-settings, telemetry-monitoring and Websites API; no such policy.

claims.claim: Diagnostic logging is configured for an individual site.
claims.quote: Select your website. ... From the Site Actions menu, select Enable diagnostics logs.

claims.claim: The admin analytics dashboard covers websites across the tenant, filtered by environment and site.
claims.quote: Each chart displays the DAU, WAU, and MAU for all the sites in the selected environment. ... Traffic reports are available only for public sites. Private sites aren't included in these reports.
claims.fix: Replace the dashboard clause with: 'The admin analytics dashboard covers public websites across the tenant, filtered by environment and Site ID; private sites are not included.'

claims.where: Governance controls: diagnostic logging storage paragraph
claims.claim: Diagnostic logging writes website error logs into an Azure Blob storage account owned by the organisation.
claims.quote: To access the logs, configure your website to send all application errors to an Azure Blob storage account that you own.
